doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Flip Benson, Grand Rapids and the Army
title: Life in Flip's band and the Springfield State Fair
summary: The band broadcasts nightly, plays only BMI tunes, and tours Quincy, Springfield and Grand Rapids until 1941; Ware hears many bands at the fair.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: music. I think during that time, ASCAP and BMI -- we had a lineup from the club, and we broadcasted every night, and so we had to play all BMI tunes. Now my ear was sharp -- I could play anything I heard, you know, we'd rehearse, but I could play it. He tried to help me in every way; he would say, "You want to learn how to read? I'll teach you."

And I was wild, and a young cat, hanging with these grownups, and I thought I was something. I didn't have time. I could play, you know? And we were playing nothing but straight ahead music. We played every kind of tune imaginable.

But I stayed with that band from the summer of '39 up until the summer of '41 -- 6 months here, 4 months here, Quincy, Illinois; Springfield, Illinois; Grand Rapids, Michigan, and then back to Quincy. The last time I played Quincy with Flip, who comes in upstairs -- because the Casino Blue Room was a big rambling nightclub where they had the Blue Room downstairs and upstairs they had the big dancehall; they'd bring bands in there, and -- Kay Kaiser, his band with Ginny Simms -- all those kind of bands would come.

And I was just happy. And when we played Springfield, Illinois, this was during the period of the Springfield State Fair -- it was another state fair -- you used to see all kinds of bands out there. Some came out of St. Louis -- Louis Armstrong had a big band come through. T-Bone Walker come through with Les Hyte's big band ... oh, so many musicians. It
was jammed all day. Go all day and come back and jam all night. And then we went to Grand Rapids, Michigan -- but that's another story.
